industry.why: Double Underweight, carried unchanged. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): the United States consumer surveys fell again (University of Michigan 46.3 preliminary October, down 1.8; Conference Board 81.9 in September, down 6.7; Goldman Sachs 19 Oct), consumer discretionary lagged with technology and communication services in the week's rotation (Jefferies, 17 Oct), and the European consumer was again not read, so the row rests on the US reading and on the regime. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: D now, D prior, the largest industry in the universe at 138 stocks. Counter-case: Retail physical reads B and Online retail A on relative strength, Hotels C, which is where cheap good businesses accumulate, and a double notch on 138 stocks shuts bottom-up work out of the Lists; the exceptions are carried at sector level (H.3 Neutral).

sector.why: Underweight. Component 1 regime (rates-led late cycle: Richard's view 16-Sep-26, rates and yields rising, inflation high, consumer confidence low, downside skew; sources absent): consumer confidence low and high multiples derate with yields. Relative strength AGREES, F now from C two months prior. Counter-case: proven brands, and a fall from C to F may already be the repricing.

geography.why: Overweight, carried unchanged. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): the Swiss index is among those Goldman (19 Oct) names as rallying alongside non-AI and low-beta exposures, which is the rotation this row was set on; the Swiss National Bank was not re-read this week, so last week's 'not hiking' stands. Relative strength is not graded by country. Counter-case unchanged: the franc takes 2 to 3 points a year off a Swiss exporter's reported profit (Sonova memo), and five of the Swiss Pool names are semiconductor names inside an Underweight sector. Back to C if the SNB joins the hikers or the franc reverses.
